messages:
Alex: quick heads-up  ran a focused CPU-side perf + flamegraph pass on the staging inference worker to investigate the tokenization + scheduler hotspots from the e2e regression. Wanted to capture the stack topoffs and see if Python overhead or our batching logic is the big culprit. :mag:

Maria: which image/commit and how did you collect?

Alex: image: inference-worker:v2024-07-22-rc3 (sha: b7f9c2) on c5d. Command I used:
```
perf record -F 99 -g -- python3 -u services/serve_entry.py --model rdx-v1 --profile --batch-size=8
perf script | ./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl > /tmp/flame.svg
```

Alex: TL;DR from the flamegraph:
- scheduler main loop (our Python loop) ~= 28% CPU
- tokenization (regex + unicodedata.normalize) ~= 15%
- grpc/uvloop syscalls ~= 8%
- libc memcpy/malloc churn around numpy/list->array boundaries

David: did you build with debug symbols? Python frames can be noisy otherwise.

Alex: rebuilt with -g and populated perf buildid-cache; symbols resolved. Also ran `python -X importtime` to rule out import-time overhead (negligible).

Maria: any link to KV cache miss patterns? last week's traces showed host stalls waiting for GPU refill.

Alex: correlated with NVTX-marked nsys traces. On KV misses host scheduler spends ~30-80ms waiting for async I/O + kernel to populate KV, but thats separate from baseline scheduler cost. The flamegraph points to a hot path: 
```
python_scheduler_loop
  -> run_forever
    -> _dispatch_batches
      -> _prepare_batch (tokenize_text -> tok.normalize -> regex.finditer)
      -> submit_to_runtime (pack_kv_requests -> serialize -> socket.send)
```

David: tokenization path is pure Python (regex + unicodedata + list comps)? We should measure switching to a C tokenizer or Rust/PyO3.

Alex: tried quick wins: replaced some `re.sub` uses with `str.translate` for ASCII folding  gave ~6% improvement on tokenization wall time. Also prototyped `tensor_builder.c` via cffi to avoid Python list->np.array copies; PoC yielded ~20% reduction on that segment.

Maria: scheduler itself showing lock contention?

Alex: perf showed `futex` contended sites and many `PyThread_acquire_lock` samples; frequent small tasks cause GIL thrashing.

Maria: that points to batching heuristic being too eager under low-latency requests. What's current heuristic?

Alex: flush when (1) tokens >= 1024 aggregate OR (2) queued requests >= 8 OR (3) time_since_first_request >= 12ms. Local tweak to queued_requests=16 cut CPU ~9% but increased tail latency for small QPS.

David: other hotspots? memcpy/pybind11 conversions?

Alex: yes, significant `memcpy`/`memmove` tied to pybind11 buffer conversions and numpy copy edges. I modified serializer to avoid copies for contiguous ASCII; saved ~4% CPU.

perf-bot: alert: nightly-regressions/rdx-inference-worker flagged +6% CPU vs baseline at 03:12 UTC. Trace link: https://internal.perf/alerts/9843 :warning:

David: GPU-side nsys traces show many short kernels (<200us) with gaps; kernel-selection currently picks single-token optimized kernels which lower per-token compute but introduce kernel launch overhead. Can we coalesce small requests into multi-token kernels?

Alex: nsys timeline shows host thread often blocked on `epoll_wait`/socket while kernels launch in bursts. Coalescing small requests might reduce kernel launch rate, but requires routing/batching changes so we don't regress latency for small interactive calls.

Maria: action items?

Alex: propose:
- short-term: bump queued_requests 8 -> 12 on canary, monitor P50/95/99, gated rollout (traffic %)
- mid-term: land tensor_builder.c PoC (PR: https://git.redwood/rdx/serve/pull/12345) as opt-in to reduce Python->C copy overhead
- infra: run combined nsys + perfetto capture during synthetic burst (tools/burst_replay.py) to get host<->GPU correlated traces
- long-term: consider moving scheduler to C++/Rust or a lightweight RPC merge service to avoid GIL and microtask overhead

David: for nsys, use `--capture-range nvtx --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --stop-on-range-end` and add NVTX markers around dispatch/kv fills. Use the synthetic burst harness.

Alex: also ran `perf record -e cycles:u -c 100000 -g` on the canary; it highlighted regex slowpaths. Rewrote a few hot regexes and saw ~6% additional improvement.

Maria: risk on canary config?

Alex: small: under very sparse QPS some micro-batches may see slightly higher tail latency. Ill gate by percent and rollback if 95th climbs >5%.

David: one more: collect `perf record -g -p <pid> -o /tmp/perf.data` live on a 1% traffic canary to get true stacks.

Alex: will do and upload flame svgs + nsys captures to the PR. Pushing canary with queued_requests=12 and opt-in tensor_builder. :eyes:

perf-bot: note: next scheduled perf collection at 02:00 UTC will include kernel-selection A/B telemetry. :white_check_mark:

Maria: great. can you drop a short summary + links (PoC + canary dashboard + flame svg) in #eng-runtime when artifacts are uploaded?

Alex: yes, will post links and the flamegraph SVG once uploads finish. Thanks all.
